candidate_068.name: coverage-preserving exploration reserve against theory-conditioned sampling lock-in
candidate_068.mechanism_hypothesis: Do not allocate the entire experiment budget to the current theories, even when discriminability-targeted experiments are locally informative. Maintain an explicitly theory-independent or weakly theory-conditioned exploration reserve over the admissible design space, plus diversity/representativeness diagnostics. Use targeted experiments to distinguish live theories, but use the reserve to detect omitted regimes, misspecification and self-confirming sampling. Promotion should depend on performance against representative or held-out coverage, not only the adaptively collected sample.

primary_evidence.source: Against theory-motivated experimentation: Can random experimental choice lead to better theories?, Dubova, Moskvichev & Zollman, Collective Intelligence 5(1), first published 16 Feb 2026, DOI 10.1177/26339137261421577
primary_evidence.design: A multi-agent computational model jointly varies active experiment choice, theory construction and social learning. Ground truths are mixtures of multivariate Gaussians with varied dimensionality/clusters; agents construct compressed theories from samples selected by random, novelty, confirmation, falsification, disagreement and hybrid strategies. Five simulation experiments vary learning time, prior training, measurement restrictions, independent/dependent-variable structure, group size/communication and epistemic objective. Actual performance is evaluated on representative samples from the full ground-truth distribution rather than only the adaptively collected data.

results.perceived_vs_actual_reversal: All theory-guided strategies fit their own collected data better than random (p<.001), but actual full-ground-truth performance reversed: random was better than all tested theory-guided strategies (p<.001). Appendix A1 actual-error coefficients versus random were +582.24 disagreement+falsification, +720.45 disagreement+confirmation, +666.92 disagreement, +656.62 falsification, +1228.46 confirmation, and +262.37 novelty, all p<.001.
results.robustness: The random strategy was best or tied for best actual ground-truth reconstruction across 50, 100, 150, 200, 250 and 300 observations and remained superior across the varied ground-truth complexity, measurement limits, communication conditions and prior-training amounts reported by the study.
results.mechanism: Theory-motivated strategies sampled narrower, less representative regions that were easier to explain, creating an illusion of epistemic success when evaluation reused the acquired sample. The paper explicitly frames this as a representativeness/sampling problem rather than a blanket rejection of all algorithmic adaptive design.

primary_evidence.interpretation: This is strong negative evidence against making candidate_066-style theory-discriminating experiment selection the sole exploration policy. It motivates a coverage-preserving exploration channel and representative/held-out adjudication so the live theory set cannot define away omitted regimes.
primary_evidence.limits: This is a stylized multi-agent simulation, not an LLM scientist or laboratory experiment. The ground truth is known to the evaluator, the scientific goal is primarily informative/predictive representation, and random sampling still depends on a pre-defined experimental space. The authors explicitly note that precise automated active-learning designs may behave differently and that theory-driven experiments can be preferable under cost or domain constraints. Therefore no universal random-fraction or blanket random-over-targeted rule is supported.

corroborating_boundary.source: Characterizing the robustness of Bayesian adaptive experimental designs to active learning bias, Sloman et al., arXiv:2205.13698
corroborating_boundary.result: Bayesian adaptive experimental design can produce inconsistent estimates under model misspecification because information-seeking sampling becomes unrepresentative; worse misspecification increases active-learning bias in the analyzed linear case and the pattern transfers to a simulated nonlinear preference-learning example.
corroborating_boundary.scope: Older non-agent adaptive-design corroboration only; it supports misspecification risk, not a particular exploration reserve size.

candidate_068.relation_to_existing: Adds a necessary anti-lock-in boundary to candidate_066's discriminability-targeted experiment generation and candidate_067's belief-sensitive filtering. Candidate_066 has direct small-n science-domain evidence that targeted experiments recover some mechanisms missed by random design; candidate_068 shows a different regime where conditioning experiment choice on current theories can systematically hide omitted structure. The unresolved design question is therefore mixture/arbitration: when to spend budget on discriminating live theories versus coverage-preserving exploration, with prospective representative adjudication.
